You're working in a NEW git worktree you should create at /opt/nxeon-wip-region-pages (branch feature/region-umbrella-pages, off latest main in /opt/nxeon). Symlink node_modules and .env from /opt/nxeon into the worktree. Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon directly, do NOT merge or deploy — make the changes, verify, and report back. Do NOT run `git add -A` (a documented past incident replaced prod's real node_modules with a self-referential symlink) — stage specific files by name only if asked to commit (only commit if explicitly asked; leave it uncommitted otherwise).

## Context

Nxeon (a VPS/hosting/game-server platform) has a live programmatic SEO system: `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` defines a typed matrix of (location × service) landing pages — 18 cities (4 in Europe: London, Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Paris; 6 in North America: New York, Toronto, Los Angeles, Dallas, Miami, Chicago; plus APAC/other: Singapore [the one REAL datacenter], Sydney, Tokyo, Mumbai, Hong Kong, Seoul, Dubai, São Paulo) crossed with 6 service types (vps/game/web/dedicated/forex/reseller) = 107 combo pages, all rendered by ONE dynamic route `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` and auto-included in `app/sitemap.ts` via the exported `LANDING_SLUGS`.

Read `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` in FULL first — it has a detailed doc comment explaining the honesty framing (`presence: "datacenter" | "network" | "market"` — Nxeon has exactly ONE real datacenter, Singapore; every other location page must never claim a literal on-site datacenter, only "market-targeting" framing with an honest FAQ answer about where servers actually run). Read `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` to understand exactly how a `LocationDef` + `ServiceDef` pair gets turned into a full page (H1, meta, OG, prose sections, why-points, steps, FAQ, internal links, pricing grid).

## The gap

All 107 existing pages are CITY-level (e.g., "New York VPS Hosting", "London VPS Hosting"). There is no broader REGION-level page for "American VPS Hosting" or "European VPS Hosting" (or the equivalent for the other 5 service types) that would catch more generic, higher-volume searches from people who don't specify a city. The owner explicitly asked for this: "I would like to also build some infrastructure SEO wise for American hosting, European hosting, etc."

## Your task

Design and build a REGION-level tier of landing pages, cleanly composed with the existing city-level system rather than duplicating it. Concretely:

1. Add a new region concept — e.g. a `RegionDef` type (region slug like "usa"/"europe", display name, the `regionLong`/audience-style prose fields analogous to `LocationDef`, and a list of which existing `LocationDef` slugs belong to that region — e.g. USA region = new-york, los-angeles, dallas, miami, chicago (NOT toronto, which is Canada); Europe region = london, frankfurt, amsterdam, paris). Think about what regions make sense given the EXISTING city roster — don't invent cities that don't already exist as LocationDefs; the region pages should aggregate/reference the real city pages already live, not fabricate new individual city claims.
2. Crossed with the same 6 `ServiceKey` types (or a sensible subset if a service type doesn't make sense at region granularity — use your judgment and justify it), generate region-level landing pages following the SAME honesty discipline as the existing system: presence is never "datacenter" for a region page (Singapore is the only one), audience/market framing throughout, an honest FAQ about where servers actually run.
3. A region page should feel genuinely different from a same-service city page, not a thin wrapper — e.g. it can reference/link to its constituent city pages ("we serve the US primarily via low-latency routes to New York, Los Angeles, Dallas, Miami and Chicago" with real internal links to those live pages), discuss the region's broader connectivity/market context, and target the more generic search query pattern ("american vps hosting", "european vps hosting", "hosting in europe") rather than duplicating a specific city's copy.
4. Decide the cleanest implementation path — e.g. extending the same dynamic `[slug]/page.tsx` route to also resolve region slugs (checking whether a slug matches a `RegionDef` first, then falling back to the existing `LocationDef` matrix), or a parallel dedicated route. Prefer extending the existing system since it already has all the SEO plumbing (metadata, OG, sitemap inclusion, schema) — don't rebuild that from scratch if you can compose with it. Update `app/sitemap.ts` accordingly so region pages are included automatically, matching how `LANDING_SLUGS` already works.
5. Every claim must be real and verifiable the same way the existing system enforces it — no fabricated stats, no invented reviews, no claimed datacenters. If you're unsure whether a specific regional/connectivity claim is defensible, phrase it generically and truthfully (e.g. "low-latency routes to major hubs across Europe" rather than a specific unverifiable latency number) rather than inventing a number.

## Test baseline

Before your changes, `npm test` has 34 pre-existing, unrelated failures (pricing/proration/auth-baseline tests) — this is the established, known baseline. Confirm your change doesn't add any NEW failures beyond that same set of 34.

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — must be clean.
2. `npm test` — compare against the 34-failure baseline, confirm zero new failures.
3. Real visual verification: run `next dev` on an isolated port, visit a couple of the new region pages directly, and screenshot them (desktop) to confirm they render correctly, look distinct from a city-level page for the same service, and internal links to constituent city pages work. This worktree's `.env` points at the LIVE production database (read-only queries for pricing data are fine and already how the existing system works) — do not run anything that writes to it. Do NOT run broad process-killing commands like `pkill -f "next dev"` — a previous agent this session did that and it matched the live production systemd service's process name pattern too; scope any process-stopping command by exact PID or port.

## Report back

Summarize: how many region pages you created and their slugs, which region/service combinations you decided to include or skip and why, how you extended (or didn't) the existing route/sitemap system, confirmation of the 3 verification steps, and leave the change uncommitted in the worktree for review (per this session's standing rule: only commit when explicitly asked).
